newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: City Developments results surprise again.
newsitem.headline: City Developments results surprise again.

text.p: Singapore's property bluechip City Developments Ltd (CityDev) surprised the market for the second year running on Wednesday with a stronger than expected performance for 1996.
The group reported a 33.8 percent rise in net profit to Singapore $535.42 million for the year ended December 31 1996.
This was sharply higher than the concensus forecast of S$483.6 million by analysts polled in the Endinbrugh Financial Publications Estimate Directory.
"The results are very good and much better than expected," said Ng Yeow Tong, investment analyst with GK Goh Securities.
He said the higher earnings were mainly from development profits from residential properties.
"They are probably recognising profits held back from previous years. This is the second year they have surprised on the upside. Hopefully, this year the market would get it right," Ng said.
To celebrate the strong performance, CityDev said it was recommending a special dividend of five percent in addition to the final dividend of 15 percent.
Analysts said the dividend payout from the group was still very low, amounting to a total of 10 cents against the company's share price of S$13.
Reviewing the group's 1996 results, CityDev said development profits continued to contribute significantly to group earnings. It had launched 1,309 new homes for sale during the year.
Rental income for the group, mainly from offices, rose 35 percent to S$168 million. Net lettable office space jumped to 1.9 million sq ft in 1996 from 1.2 million the previous year.

The group's hotel operations, held mainly through CDL Hotels International Ltd, also had a strong year with turnover rising 41 percent to S$886 million and pretax profit up 67 percent to S$147 million.
CDL's successful floatation of Millennium & Copthorne Plc in London during the year resulted in a profit of 12 million pounds sterling or S$27.6 million.
The group said it expected to perform well in 1997.
